fields.reasoning: Intent: milestone-25 (the daemon builds and ships the backlog on its own) is still open and is what CI failures on model and generated-file errors stall; the predecessor ship-local-gate served it, and milestone-32 is about cleanup and language-neutral defaults, which this change only has to respect. Enforcement: the owner wants every push covered (fixer, ci-fix, merge-of-main pushes, plan runs). Workflow steps alone would need a gate before each push step in five builtin workflows and any custom one, and the three failing PRs came from plan runs that have no gate at all; pushes in code all go through shipPush (internal/api/ship_close.go, called by ship_openpr.go and the land) and ship_rebase.go's push, so a check there cannot be skipped by a workflow that forgets a step, and the push step's failure is already routed by on.fail. Name: existing per-project command settings are rhiza.ship.localGate and rhiza.ship.generate (ship_gate.go, ship_generate.go); rhiza.ship.prePushCheck follows that prefix, says when it runs, and names no language or tool, as milestone-32 asks. Plan fixer: plan.toml's revise step is tied to review findings and loops back to review, and its cap of 2 is shared with them; pre-push failures in plans are model errors (duplicate handle, non-canonical log entry, stale render) a dedicated small fixer step can repair with rhiza apply or rhiza render, matching the intent's point (4) that a failure goes back to a fixer within the step's cap instead of pushing.
fields.statement: Change set 01M76RH0 serves @{01M6HKVRE1B7RPP12EN6J2GGXC}, as its predecessor @{01M6YCRKT22SQQH70HYX1GPFZW} did, and only coordinates with @{01M7640BA83BXBMSEMZNC4K97G} by keeping the new setting language neutral. The pre-push check is enforced in the product, in one shared helper run before every git push a run makes (shipPush, used by ship open-pr and the land push; ship rebase's push; and the watchdog's merge-of-main push in watchdogMergeMain), so plan, plan-milestone, ship-change and its wrappers such as bugfix all get it, including fixer, ci-fix and merge-of-main pushes; it runs rhiza check on the run worktree, then the project's command, and a failure refuses the push and fails that step with the failing lines, recorded in the run journal and rhiza run status. The setting is rhiza.ship.prePushCheck, a project setting with an empty default (rhiza check alone), set to make self-check for this repo, beside rhiza.ship.localGate and rhiza.ship.generate. rhiza.ship.localGate keeps its meaning (only while CI is unstable). In ship-change a push step failed by the pre-push check goes on.fail through a rhiza ship gate --failed triage, as rebase does today, to the existing gate-fix fixer, within its cap; other failures of those steps end the run as today. The plan and plan-milestone workflows each get the same triage and one new agent fixer step for it (for example prepush-fix, max_visits 2) that fixes the plan's model or rendered files from the failing lines with one rhiza apply or rhiza render and goes back to open-pr; conflicts and gh or push errors still end the run, and once its cap is spent the run fails as a failing step does today.

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run 'TestShipPrePushCheck|TestShipLocalGate|TestWatchdogPRNoCI' passes, showing in a run worktree with a non-canonical log entry, a stale render, or a failing prePushCheck command that ship open-pr, ship land, ship rebase and the watchdog's merge of origin/main each push nothing to origin and fail with the failing lines in their error and response (the watchdog leaving the branch at its pre-merge head), that with both passing they push as before (CI stable or unstable), and that localGate still runs only while CI is unstable
fields.statement: Before every git push a run makes (shipPush, used by ship open-pr and the land push; ship rebase's push of a merged head; and the watchdog's merge of origin/main into a run's branch, watchdogMergeMain in internal/api/watchdog_noci.go), all through one shared helper, whatever CI's state, Rhiza runs rhiza check on the run's worktree (model, log canonicity, stale render) and then the project's rhiza.ship.prePushCheck command there; if either fails it pushes nothing and fails the step with the failing lines (the watchdog resets its merge as on a failed push and reports the failing lines), while rhiza.ship.localGate keeps running only while CI is unstable

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/workflow/... passes, checking that ship-change.toml's open-pr, push-merge and land go on.fail to a ship gate --failed triage whose on.pass is gate-fix (gate-fix-merge for land) and which has no on.fail, that rebase still reaches gate-fix through rebase-triage and rebase-gate-failed, and that gate-fix's and gate-fix-merge's max_visits are unchanged; go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run TestShipGate passes, showing ship gate --failed passing on a head the pre-push check failed on and failing after an open-pr or land failure that was not the pre-push check (a gh or push error)
fields.statement: In the built-in ship-change workflow (and its wrappers such as bugfix), open-pr, push-merge and land, which have no on.fail today, each go on.fail to a triage step running rhiza ship gate --failed, as rebase does through rebase-triage and rebase-gate-failed; it passes only on a head the pre-push check (or local gate) failed on and then goes to the existing gate-fix fixer (gate-fix-merge after land) within its cap, and any other failure of those steps (gh, network, git) fails the triage with no on.fail and ends the run as today; ship gate --failed reports a head the pre-push check failed on, and the fixers' prompt reads the failing pre-push lines as well as a failing local gate's

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/workflow/... passes, checking that plan.toml and plan-milestone.toml route open-pr's and rebase's on.fail to a ship gate --failed triage whose on.pass is prepush-fix and which has no on.fail, that prepush-fix has max_visits 2 and on.pass open-pr, and that rhiza workflow describe plan lists both steps; go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run TestShipGate passes, showing ship gate --failed failing on a ship rebase conflict and on a gh or push error; make self-check passes
fields.statement: The built-in plan and plan-milestone workflows each send open-pr's and rebase's failure (both have no on.fail today) to a triage step running rhiza ship gate --failed, which passes only on a head the pre-push check failed on and then goes to a new agent step, prepush-fix (max_visits 2), that fixes the plan's model or rendered files from the failing lines with one rhiza apply or rhiza render and goes back to open-pr; any other failure (a conflicting merge of main, a gh or push error) fails the triage with no on.fail and ends the run as today, and once prepush-fix's cap is spent the run fails as a failing step does today
